# Wire protocol reference

Every table on this page is extracted from source, not transcribed. See
[`tools/gen_protocol_reference.py`](https://github.com/Tinkerbug-Robotics/TinkerRocket/blob/main/tools/gen_protocol_reference.py)
for which file each one comes from. For how the links are used, see
[Protocols](../protocols.md).

## Frame format

Inter-board frames (FC↔OC over I2C and I2S, and the on-flash log) share one
framing:

```
[0xAA 0x55 0xAA 0x55] [Type] [Length] [Payload] [CRC16_MSB] [CRC16_LSB]
   (start of frame)    (1)     (1)     (0-N)     (1)         (1)
```

Start-of-frame bytes from [`TR_I2C_Interface.h`](https://github.com/Tinkerbug-Robotics/TinkerRocket/blob/main/tinkerrocket-idf/components/TR_I2C_Interface/TR_I2C_Interface.h).

## FC ↔ OC message types

two handlers sharing a value means the second is silently dead — which is why
this list is CI-enforced for uniqueness.

> 53 of these 90 codes carry no comment in the header,
> so the Notes column is blank for them. Direction is inferred from the
> `_PENDING` / `_CMD` / `_MSG` suffix in that case, which is a convention,
> not a guarantee. A trailing `// OC→FC: what it does` on the constant
> fills the row in.

## BLE command spaces

The app talks to **either** an Out Computer or a Base Station, so the two
spaces are independent and values may overlap: command 50 is mag-cal start to
the Out Computer and relay-to-rocket to the Base Station. Both are guarded
for internal uniqueness by [`tools/check_ble_command_ids.py`](https://github.com/Tinkerbug-Robotics/TinkerRocket/blob/main/tools/check_ble_command_ids.py).

## Sensor health field

Two bits per sensor at the shifts below, each holding a `SensorHealthState`
(`SH_NA` 0, `SH_OK` 1, `SH_DEGRADED` 2, `SH_BAD` 3).

| Shift | Name | Covers |
|-------|------|--------|
| 0 | `SH_BARO_SHIFT` |  |
| 2 | `SH_IMU_SHIFT` |  |
| 4 | `SH_EKF_SHIFT` | EKF filter health: init + isHealthy + covariance converged |
| 6 | `SH_MAG_SHIFT` |  |
| 8 | `SH_GNSS_SHIFT` |  |
| 10 | `SH_BATT_SHIFT` | set by the OC from POWERData |
| 12 | `SH_PYRO_SHIFT[0]` | pyro channel 1 |
| 14 | `SH_PYRO_SHIFT[1]` | pyro channel 2 |
| 16 | `SH_PYRO_SHIFT[2]` | pyro channel 3 |
| 18 | `SH_PYRO_SHIFT[3]` | pyro channel 4 |
| 20 | `SH_STORAGE_SHIFT` |  |
| 22 | `SH_GNSS_ABSENT_SHIFT` |  |
